Detect Colliding Evidence Rows

Source: R/evidence_schema.R
evidence_collisions.Rd

Finds rows in an evidence table that share the same key and reports them. By default the key is the (indicator_id, asset_id, location) triple that identifies a single finding on a single place in an asset, so more than one row on that key is a duplicate that assembling adapters can introduce. A collision is a conflict when the colliding rows disagree on their outcome, that is when they carry more than one distinct value in conflict_on (result by default).

Usage

evidence_collisions(
  ev,
  keys = c("indicator_id", "asset_id", "location"),
  conflict_on = "result"
)

Arguments

ev

A valid evidence data.frame.

keys

Character vector of column names forming the collision key. Defaults to c("indicator_id", "asset_id", "location").

conflict_on

Single column name whose distinct values decide whether a collision is a conflict. Defaults to "result".

Value

A data.frame with one row per colliding key (keys appearing on more than one row), ordered by the key columns. It has the keys columns plus n (number of rows on the key), n_distinct (distinct non-NA values of conflict_on), conflict (logical, TRUE when n_distinct > 1), and values (the distinct conflict_on values, comma separated). A table with no collisions yields a zero-row frame with these columns.

Details

This is purely structural: it groups rows and counts distinct values. It applies no weights, thresholds, or scoring and makes no judgement about which row is correct.

See also

bind_evidence(), which uses this to report and optionally resolve collisions while combining tables.

Examples

ctx <- suppressMessages(r4sub_run_context("STUDY1", "DEV"))
ev <- suppressMessages(as_evidence(
  data.frame(
    asset_type = "validation", asset_id = rep("ADSL", 3),
    source_name = c("p21", "p21", "other"),
    indicator_id = c("SD0001", "SD0001", "SD0002"),
    indicator_name = c("SD0001", "SD0001", "SD0002"),
    indicator_domain = "quality", severity = "high",
    result = c("fail", "warn", "pass"), location = c("AGE", "AGE", "SEX"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ),
  ctx = ctx
))
evidence_collisions(ev)
#>   indicator_id asset_id location n n_distinct conflict     values
#> 1       SD0001     ADSL      AGE 2          2     TRUE fail, warn
